short: The only full fleet action of the war, and an argument ever since about who won it.
full:
On 31 May 1916 Admiral Scheer took the High Seas Fleet to sea hoping to trap and destroy part of Britain's Grand Fleet. Room 40's codebreakers gave warning and Jellicoe sailed first. The battlecruiser squadrons met that afternoon off the Jutland Bank, and three British battlecruisers blew up when flash from turret hits reached their magazines, prompting Beatty's remark that there seemed to be something wrong with his ships.

Jellicoe twice crossed the German T in the evening, and both times Scheer escaped behind smoke and destroyer attacks using a practised simultaneous turn away. Confused night actions cost the British further losses, and by dawn the Germans were home. Britain lost fourteen ships and over 6,000 men to Germany's eleven ships and around 2,500. Berlin claimed victory on the arithmetic. Strategically it was nothing of the kind: the High Seas Fleet never again seriously challenged the blockade, and Germany turned instead to unrestricted submarine warfare.
